accounts.name: user
docs: Not required to sign. The partner_admin is the authorizing party here.

accounts.name: collection
docs: credentials. We can't use a typed Anchor account here because mpl-core
isn't Anchor-native, so the handler checks the owner, the account type,
and the update authority by hand before trusting it.

accounts.name: user
docs: audit trail. Doesn't sign. Authorization comes from the attestor
(via has_one on Partner) and the Enrollment PDA that partner_admin

accounts.name: user
docs: Authorization chains back through the Enrollment PDA that start_attempt
required, which in turn required partner_admin to sign enroll_user.
The attestor can't write scores against an arbitrary pubkey because
the Attempt PDA won't exist unless start_attempt already succeeded
for that user, and start_attempt won't succeed without a live
Enrollment. So the user's consent comes from the partner's maker-
checker enrollment decision, not from a direct user signature here.
